liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Playing In The Band** (3 reviews): Reviewer's highlight: mellow, then spacey, then Phil battling giant dinosaurs before resolving into a beautiful jam; Playin' melts down and gets so far out it sounds like a fight with aliens or dinosaurs [7][8][15]
- **Let It Grow** (2 reviews): Reviewer says the long first set meant it ended a little short of complete; Reviewer calls it phenomenal [12][14]
- **Mind Left Body Jam** (2 reviews): Emerges from space, likened to someone making noise with a deflating balloon; Named among the reviewer's favorite moments alongside Playin' in the Band [10][16]
- **Dire Wolf** (1 review): Reviewer calls this a real funky version [9]
- **Beer Barrel Polka** (1 review): Reviewer was surprised the band played a polka other than Mexicali; found it very groovy [12]
- **Weather Report Suite Part 1** (1 review): Described as flawless, closing out the first set [7]
- **Wharf Rat** (1 review): Reviewer says it is played perfectly [9]
- **Mississippi Half-Step Uptown Toodeloo** (1 review): Transition from Half-Step into Playin' sounds like something rehearsed hundreds of times [10]

## The recordings

- **gd73-12-02.aud.vernon.17278.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): audience recording; 27 songs; 186 min; rated 4.89/5 by 27 [1]. Said about its sound: Audience source sounds pretty good; suggests slight cut near 2k, small boost at 8k and around 125 [8]
- **gd1973-12-02.sbd.clugston.lai.4733.sbefail.shnf**: soundboard; 24 songs; 183 min; rated 4.75/5 by 4 [2]
- **gd73-12-02.sbd.clugston.3415.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 24 songs; 183 min; rated 4.09/5 by 11 [3]. Said about its sound: Reviewer hears the soundboard as warm, dark and very mellow overall; Bass and rhythm come across hypnotically on the soundboard, especially in Weather Report; audience tape's quality adds strange ambience [7][9]
- **gd1973-12-02.150276.s2.sbd.miller.flac1648**: soundboard; 10 songs; 107 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [5]
- **gd1973-12-02.aud.degen.partial.110782.flac1644**: audience recording; 7 songs; 29 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [6]. Said about its sound: Sound is pretty clear, suggesting the taper sat close to the stage [6]

## Around the show

- Crowd is partial to the party; the Half-Step ending brought high fives among strangers [12]
- Listener asks about Phil apparently requesting a spotlight on someone in row four during banter [16]
- Lean five-piece lineup, since Donna was off tour, close to giving birth [18]
- At the end of Ramble On Rose, Phil talks at length about tunes played [18]
- Taper seated near stage was spotted by Sam Cutler, who yanked the mic down and stopped the recording [6]
- Reviewer ranks the Playin' among the best of 1973, with an average first set [8]
- Reviewer says it would be the benchmark of all 1973 shows if not for the cut-and-paste official release [11]
- Reviewer ranks it top five of 1973, edging 11/30 and well ahead of 12/1 [15]
- Second night of a two-night Boston Music Hall run, following 11/30/73 [18]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd73-12-02.aud.vernon.17278.sbeok.shnf**: taped by Unknown; transferred by Matt Vernon and Marc Pujol; source: Audience Recording [1]
- **gd1973-12-02.sbd.clugston.lai.4733.sbefail.shnf**: transferred by Scott Clugston; source: Master Soundboard Reel > Cassette > DAT > CDR [2]. Also: Soundboard transferred with EAC and shorten by Scott Clugston; hosted by Mike Lai; some overlap between discs 2 and 3 [2]
- **gd73-12-02.sbd.clugston.3415.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [3]. Also: The official release chopped up the show; reviewer wants the unused leftovers posted, and notes the audience recording exists [11]
- **gd1973-12-02.150276.s2.sbd.miller.flac1648**: transferred by All Transfers and Mastering by Charlie Miller  June 23, 2020; source: SBD > Master Reel > DAT (48k) [5]. Also: Soundboard source from the show featured on Dick's Picks 14; Sugar Magnolia comes from a cassette generation [5]
- **gd1973-12-02.aud.degen.partial.110782.flac1644**: taped by Unknown; transferred by Andrew F.; source: FOB AUD Source: Unknown equipment > MAC taped by Bill Degen. This transfer is 1st Gen cassette, kindly provided by Tim Friend. [6]. Also: Partial audience recording came as filler on first-generation tapes of Degen and Friend's 12-01-1973 [6]
